summary: Phramaha Niras Ruangsan works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned an MBS (2009) and PhD (2015) at the University of Sydney under Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, Peter Oldmeadow, Mark Allon, and Prayong Seanburan, and held a doctorate post at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University in 2017.

Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under traditional teacher Phrathepyanmahamuni and completed a PhD at the University of Sydney (attested 2009) supervised by Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle.
Phrapongsak K. is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts in 2015 as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and an open-call researcher at the Buddhist Art and Culture Research Center.

Phuntsok Tashi works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a BA at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and an MA at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff works in Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After earning her PhD at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (1973), she served as professor at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and later at Yale University (2004).
Pia Guerrini Bione (1884–1971) was an Indology scholar who studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa and its Classe di Lettere e Filosofia, earning her doctorate in 1907.

Linguist Pier Gabriele Goidanich (1868–1953) studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore and the University of Milan under Graziadio Isaia Ascoli. He served as professor at the University of Pisa and later held professorships at the University of Bologna from ~1904 to 1938.

Piero Martinetti (1872–1943) worked in philosophy and Indology, earning his PhD at the University of Turin under Giovanni Flechia before studying at Leipzig. He served as professor at the Accademia Scientifico-Letteraria di Milano and the University of Milan (1906–1931).
Pierre Arènes is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under André Bareau and held an attested post at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique (2003–2004).

Pierre Bourdieu (1930–2002) studied at the École Normale Supérieure under Émile Benveniste. He later held academic posts at the Faculty of Arts of Paris, Lille University of Science and Technology, the EHESS, and the Collège de France (1981–2001).

Pierre Chantraine (1899–1974) was a linguist who studied under Ernout, Meillet, Vendryes, and Bloch. He served as directeur d’études at the EPHE (1928–1969) and professor at the Sorbonne and University of Paris (1938–1969).
Pierre Charles Olloba d'Ochoa (1816–1846) was an Indologist who studied at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales under Garcin de Tassy in 1839.

Pierre Dupont (1908–1955) was a scholar of Indology and archaeology. He studied at the EPHE and École du Louvre under Lévi, Foucher, Picard, and Stern, later working at the EFEO (1936–1950) and as professor at the Sorbonne (1950).

Pierre Fabricius (1912–1988) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Heinrich Zimmer, Walther Schubring, Sylvain Lévi, Alfred Foucher, and Louis Renou across Heidelberg, Hamburg, Paris, and SOAS, later serving as professor at the Royal University of Phnom Penh (1965–1974).

Pierre Fallon (1912–1985) studied at KU Leuven and the University of Calcutta, working in Indology and religious studies. He taught at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai, served as professor of French literature at the University of Calcutta, and founded Shanti Bhavan and Shanti Sadan.

Pierre Herman Leonard Eggermont (1914–1995) was an Indologist and historian. He earned his PhD at Leiden under F. D. K. Bosch, worked at the University of Amsterdam (1966–1979), and was a professor at KU Leuven (1969–1984).

Pierre Johanns (1881–1955) studied at KU Leuven and Oxford (Th.D.), working in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He taught philosophy at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai and St. Mary's College, Kurseong (1921–1938), and later taught Sanskrit at the University of Namur (~1939–1955).

Pierre Meile (1911–1963) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at ENS and Visva-Bharati under Lévi, Foucher, Meillet, Benveniste, Varma, and Saksena. He served as professor at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from 1939 to 1963.

Pierre Rolland (d. 1974) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Louis Renou, Armand Minard, and Karl Hoffmann, earning degrees from the University of Paris and Aix-Marseille. He worked as a researcher at the CNRS starting in 1969.

Pierre Rossillon (1874–1947) was a religious studies and Indology figure ordained as a priest with the Missionaries of Saint Francis de Sales in 1898, later serving as Bishop of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Visakhapatnam from 1926 to 1947.
